blocks.text: Validate config first, start with `--wait`, then verify bottom-up: database, migrations, vector store, API from the host and from inside the network, then an end-to-end ingest and query.

$ printf '%s' 'devpass' > secrets/db_password.txt
$ docker compose config --quiet && echo OK
$ docker compose up -d --build --wait
$ docker compose ps
rag-api-1      Up (healthy)   127.0.0.1:8000->8000/tcp
rag-db-1       Up (healthy)   127.0.0.1:5432->5432/tcp
rag-migrate-1  Exited (0)                                  # expected: one-shot
rag-qdrant-1   Up (healthy)   127.0.0.1:6333->6333/tcp

$ docker compose exec db psql -U app -d rag -c '\dx vector' -c '\d chunks'
$ docker compose logs migrate | tail -2
$ curl -s localhost:6333/readyz
$ curl -s localhost:8000/readyz
$ docker compose exec api python -c "import socket; print(socket.gethostbyname('db'))"
$ curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/ingest -F file=@samples/handbook.md
$ curl -s -X POST localhost:8000/query -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"question":"refund policy?"}'

items: `printf`, not `echo`, for secret files (no trailing newline).
Put the last checks in `scripts/smoke.sh` and run it in CI after `up --wait`.
`down` keeps data; `down -v` wipes pgdata, qdrant_storage and hf_cache.

blocks.text: Q: "How do you verify a multi-service stack actually works?" A: "Validate the merged config, start with up --wait so health gates pass, then test bottom-up: DB and extension, migration logs, vector store readiness, API readiness from the host and name resolution from inside, and finally a real ingest and query, scripted as a CI smoke test."
